name: org.machanism.machai:machai-mcp-server
description: Machai MCP Server is a Java 17 command-line application and server integration for publishing Machai functional tools, prompts, and supported resources through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It discovers compatible implementations from additional runtime JARs, translates their parameter metadata into MCP JSON schemas, and routes MCP invocations to the underlying tool functions. The artifact deliberately supplies server orchestration rather than domain tools, so teams can deploy custom automation, coding, data, or internal-platform tools independently. Its org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer entry point supports local synchronous STDIO operation, Jetty-hosted stateless HTTP, and streamable session-aware HTTP. It accepts server metadata, a project execution directory, a properties configuration file, an HTTP port, and transport selection options. This makes the artifact suitable for desktop AI clients, MCP inspectors, remote agents, and reusable GenAI tool gateways.

usageContext: Publish separately packaged Machai functional tools and prompts to MCP clients
Launch a local STDIO process from a desktop MCP client
Host stateless or streamable HTTP MCP endpoints
Provide a workspace directory as execution context for tools

constructors.description: Creates a stateless HTTP MCP server. Configure its port and project directory before loading tools and starting the Jetty-backed transport.

examples.description: Creates a stateless server with a client-visible name, a port, and a tool workspace. Use the CLI entry point for normal deployments because it performs discovery and startup.

constructors.description: Creates a streamable session-aware HTTP MCP server that can expose independently packaged Machai tools and prompts.

examples.description: Creates the streamable HTTP transport server. The corresponding deployment invocation uses org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer with --port and --session.

constructors.description: Creates a synchronous MCP server that communicates through the hosting process standard input and standard output.

examples.description: Creates a STDIO server with workspace context. Desktop client integrations normally invoke org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer instead.

features.name: main
features.signature: public static void main(java.lang.String[] args) throws java.lang.Exception
features.description: Starts the MCP server and selects a transport. No port uses STDIO, --port uses stateless HTTP, and --port with --session uses streamable HTTP. The CLI also configures name, version, project directory, and properties-file location.

examples.snippet: java -cp machai-mcp-server.jar;team-tools.jar org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer --projectDir C:/work/app --config C:/config/mcp.properties --name team-mcp --version 1.0.0 --port 45000 --session
examples.description: Install Java 17, download a release or build it with mvn -Ppack install, and place the server JAR plus a Machai functional-tool JAR on the classpath. Configure any tool credentials, then run this command to host streamable HTTP MCP on port 45000. On Unix-like systems, use : rather than ; as the classpath separator.

features.name: getConfigurator
features.signature: public static org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.PropertiesConfigurator getConfigurator(java.lang.String configFile) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Creates the properties configurator used for tool loading. A null path tries the default mcp.properties file and tolerates its absence; an explicitly supplied unreadable path throws java.io.IOException.

examples.description: Loads an explicit configuration before a custom integration. CLI deployments obtain the same behavior with --config C:/config/mcp.properties.

features.name: toHumanReadable
features.description: Converts a Machai tool name into its lower-case kebab-case MCP-facing name, for example createReleaseNotes becomes create-release-notes.

examples.description: Returns create-release-notes while adapting a custom tool. Discovery performs this naming conversion automatically in ordinary deployments.

customizations.name: Runtime functional tool libraries
customizations.description: Extend the server by packaging Machai-compatible functional tool and prompt implementations in separate JARs with their required service-provider registration. Add the JARs to the runtime classpath and the server discovers them as MCP capabilities.

examples.description: Publishes a team tool JAR through stateless HTTP MCP. After startup, configure a client to connect to http://localhost:45000/mcp.

customizations.name: Command-line transport and context configuration
customizations.description: Use -d or --projectDir for workspace context, -c or --config for properties, -n or --name and -v or --version for server metadata, -p or --port for HTTP, and -s or --session for streamable HTTP. Without -p, STDIO is selected.

examples.description: Configures a stateless HTTP server with explicit workspace context and a client-visible name.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.AbstractMcpServer
studs.description: Common MCP server contract that stores project-directory context and requires transport implementations to register tools and start the selected server.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.AbstractMcpServer.ToolSpecificationBuilder
studs.description: Transport boundary for creating MCP-specific tool specifications from generic tool definitions and invocation handlers.

examples.title: Install and run a local STDIO MCP server
steps: Install Java 17 or a newer compatible Java runtime.
Download the release JAR from SourceForge or build from source with mvn -Ppack install.
Obtain a Machai-compatible functional-tool JAR that includes its service-provider registration.
Configure credentials, model settings, and environment variables required by the selected tools.
Configure a desktop MCP client to launch java -cp machai-mcp-server.jar;functional-tool-container.jar org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer.
Launch the client and verify that its tool and prompt lists contain the discovered capabilities.
examples.description: STDIO is selected because no --port option is passed. This installation pattern is for a local MCP client that starts the Java process; use : instead of ; as the classpath separator on Unix-like systems.

examples.title: Install, configure, and use an HTTP MCP endpoint
steps: Install Java 17 and obtain the server JAR and at least one functional-tool JAR.
Create an optional mcp.properties file or prepare the properties-file path needed by the tools.
Connect MCP Inspector, mcp-remote, or another MCP client to http://localhost:45000/mcp.
Inspect the published capabilities and invoke a tool. Add --session during startup when the client requires streamable HTTP transport.
examples.description: This scenario hosts stateless HTTP MCP and passes a known workspace to tools. The deployed functional-tool libraries remain responsible for their own credentials and backing services.
